# NOTES (for later QA on the two texts; not a summary of the request)

## BOOK 1 of 2: "The Fatal Three" (Mary Elizabeth Braddon, 3 vols; Gutenberg 75410-75412)

**Vol I, Book the First: "Clotho; or Spinning the Thread"**
- Ch I "We Have Been So Happy": Drawing-room, Upper Parchment Street (Park Lane/Grosvenor Sq). John Fausset (middle-aged, stout, ex-wholesale silk merchant, firm near St Paul's Churchyard, factory at Lyons; wealthy). Wife Maud (Hon. Maud Donfrey, 3rd dau. of Lord Castle-Connell, Irish peer; 19 at marriage, married 9 yrs; blonde, languid). Daughter Mildred, 7, doll (wax-and-bran; Paris walking-talking doll). Fausset asks Maud to adopt orphan ward Fay (~13-14, "heiress", Fausset is sole trustee; will be 20 in 5 yrs). Maud objects; Mildred pleads "Let the little girl come, mother." Fausset: "Wisdom has spoken..."
- Ch II "Fay": Fay arrives from Streatham Common (suburban school, Miss Constable, proprietress; expelled-ish). Thin, pale, olive complexion, great black eyes, badly dressed. Fay & Mildred bond instantly. Fay to sleep in "Bell's room" (servant room, mews-facing). Maud dislikes Fay ("owl in an ivy-bush"). Fay: "I hate them" (lessons), loves books.
- Ch III "A Superior Person": Bell (Martha Bell, 48, ex-wet-nurse to Maud, Patrick Bell husband, Limerick lace-maker, Castle-Connell lodge). Bell hostile to Fay; "I" emphasis. Miss Colville = morning governess. Fausset says Fay's future is provided for.
- Ch IV "All She Could Remember": Fay's memories: childhood cottage on windy hill by sea (Nounou, hens, cow), "Where do they go?"; school in Streatham (Miss Constable). Fay's stories/music for Mildred. Bell eavesdrops: Meta (German maid) and Bell say Fay & Mildred are sisters; Bell: Fausset was the father. Scarlet fever at The Hook (Mildred ill; Fay nurses her). "Mamma, why mayn't I call Fay sister?" Maud: "Bell is an impertinent person." Fay: "I hate everybody else in this house." Maud: "wicked, ungrateful girl". Fausset: "She was once near and dear to me." Mildred sent to Eastbourne; Fay sent to finishing-school at Brussels; "Fay is dreadfully backward..." Maud's letter.
- Ch V "Without the Wolf": Greswold family, Enderby Manor (Hampshire, near Romsey; Test river; Dr Hutchinson of Southampton). George Greswold (adopted name; born George Ransome), Mildred Greswold (née Fausset, now ~31 later), daughter Lola (Laura), 12, golden hair, blue eyes, Latin/music. Fever in village: Johnny Giles, Mary Martin, Mrs Peter & children, Janet Dawson, Andrew Rogers, Mary Rainbow ("Polly", flaxen-haired, pitcher of milk). Dr Porter (village doctor). Bailiff Thomas; dairyman Wadman & wife Mrs Wadman; dairy fed by old garden well (manure heap contamination). Greswold insists on Scotland trip; Lola took beef tea to cottages, "Red Riding Hood, only without the wolf." Bell (Mrs Bell, 74 at that time, Lola's nurse).
- Ch VI "Ah! Pity! The Lily is Withered": Mildred in garden; Lola ill (typhoid-like). Greswold at cedar; graveyard of "widow of Nain" thoughts. Polly Rainbow dies; Mrs Rainbow: "She was all I had." Lola dies, funeral bell 10 days later. Greswold: "Judgment"-ish despair. Dairy staff dismissed.
- Ch VII "Drifting Apart": Greswolds at Lake of Thun villa. Greswold's "bad dream" ("The cage—the cage again—iron bars—like a wild beast!"). Mildred's backstory: Fay sent to Brussels; Maud died ~ Mildred 16 (heart disease), revealed Fay was Fausset's natural daughter; "Don't call her your sister." Mildred's grief; Fausset's Leipzig/Paris trip. Mildred wonders about Fay's mother.
- Ch VIII "Such Things Were": Greswold (Ransome) met Mildred at The Hook (age 17, he 30ish); Oxford friend of Fausset; George Ransome of Magdalen; brother Randolph (elder), mother's will left Enderby to George. Back at Manor after Lola's death; Mildred visits grave (white marble cross, "Laura, the only child of George and Mildred Greswold, aged twelve"). Greswold at unnamed grave: "Judgment! judgment!"
- Ch IX "The Face in the Church": Sunday; Mildred sees stranger, auburn hair, pointed beard, reddish-brown eyes (Judas-like). Greswold's niece Pamela Ransome (daughter of Randolph; sister Rosalind, Lady Mountford; Box the fox-terrier) invited to Enderby. Greswold's first marriage revealed only obliquely.
- Ch X "There Is Always the Skeleton": Stranger = César Castellani (Milanese, tenor, pianist, author of *Nepenthe*), guest at Riverdale (Tom Hillersdon & Louise Hillersdon, ex-Louise Lorraine courtesan). Castellani calls on Mildred with letter from Diana Tomkison (Cecilia Tomkison's friend), reveals Fausset/Felix silk ties. Tells Mildred Greswold's first marriage in Nice (Vivien/Ransome) & that Greswold "met at Lady Lochinvar's palace at Nice". Mildred faints/shock.
- Ch XI "The Beginning of Doubt": Greswold admits earlier concealment; "such things were". Pamela's wedding plans, Castellani's visits; Pamela's crush on Castellani. Mildred suspects concealment.
- Ch XII "She Cannot Be Unworthy": Castellani visits; plans Mr Cancellor (Clement Cancellor, Vicar of St Elizabeth's, Parchment Street, Mildred's old tutor) visiting Riverdale; Louise Hillersdon introduced.
- Ch XIII "Shall She Be Less Than Another?": Louise's backstory; Cancellor's Deceased Wife's Sister's Bill debate at Enderby (Greswold: "Shall Rachel be withheld…"; Rollinson the curate: "wouldn't be a second mother-in-law"). Charity concert at Enderby (Burne-Jones window fund), Castellani & Pamela sing.
- Ch XIV "Lifting the Curtain": Castellani hints at first wife's death "infinitely sad". Mildred confronts Greswold in library; shows photograph of first wife (small face, large dark eyes). Mildred faints.

**Vol II, Book the Second: "Lachesis; or the Meter of Destiny"**
- Ch I "A Wife and No Wife": Castellani's social standing (Magnus Dudley poet; Cavour rumours). Mildred flees Enderby by train from Romsey; Ivy Cottage; Mrs Tomkison (Cecilia, Queen Anne's Gate, husband Adam) in London. Mildred's letter to Greswold: sister-in-law claim; Greswold's fainting-fit question.
- Ch II "The Sins of the Fathers": Greswold reads letter; recalls first wife Vivien Faux (Florence, Mortimer artist couple, 1868 death). Bell interrogated: Fay "the image of him." Greswold: "Sisters!"
- Ch III "The Verdict of Her Church": Mildred to Waterloo; Cancellor advises she is legally free but morally bound to leave. Miss Gertrude Fausset (aunt) at Lewes Crescent, Brighton.
- Ch IV "No Light": Aunt Gertrude's house; Franz (Swiss butler), Louisa (maid). Aunt denies knowledge; Mildred stays; Castellani appears at aunt's; plays Mozart/Verdi-like music; aunt's musical sympathy.
- Ch V "The Future Might Be Darker": Greswold in London; Messrs Pergament & Pergament (Lincoln's Inn Fields) refuse information; Mr Pergament (bald, ~45) knows Ransome name; Vivien's Consols £30,000 income. Greswold tells Pamela; Mildred leaves? Greswold & Mildred's farewell at Brighton: "The future might be still darker..." Mr Maltravers (Vicar of St Edmund's, Brighton) and Rev. Percival Cromer.
- Ch VI "Higher Views": Mildred ill (low fever); Castellani and Pamela; Mildred plans to Pallanza/Italy; Maltravers' transept scheme; Miss Fausset's "make up your mind." Castellani's proposal refused by Mildred (Pallanza); "Yes, to a madman and a murderer."
- Ch VII "The Time Has Come": Castellani's visits; Mildred goes to Genoa & Nice; Castellani's "magnetic" vanity; Castellani slanders Greswold (Ransome lunatic in asylum near Nice, suspected of murdering wife at St Jean).
- Ch VIII "Not Proven": Mildred to Nice; Lady Lochinvar (Palais Montano); Le Bout du Monde villa at St Jean; cliff where Vivien died; Monsieur Leroy asylum doctor (Villefranche/St André road); Maria Castellani (singer); verdict: "not proven."
- Ch IX "Looking Back": Mildred at Villa Montfleuri (old Le Bout du Monde); market-woman; she visits asylum; kneels at Ransome's cell.

**Vol III, Book the Third: "Atropos; or That Which Must Be"**
- Ch I "A Wrecked Life": Maria Castellani at Leroy's house, sings Lucrezia; Mildred learns Castellani cheated Maria; Pamela & Lady Lochinvar; Mr Stuart (Malcolm Stuart, Lady Lochinvar's nephew, sandy/ginger, Highland).
- Ch II "In the Morning of Life": Greswold's solitude at Enderby; Vivien Faux backstory (Milan/Florence, Signora Vicenti party; Mortimers; Delia Darcy; marriage; St Jean villa; picnic quarrel).
- Ch III "The Rift in the Lute": St Jean villa; Vivien's jealousy; Delia Darcy & Irish sister on the common; cliff quarrel; Vivien flings herself over cliff (April 24, 1868).
- Ch IV "Darkness": Ransome rescues body; inquest at Villefranche; imprisoned; madness (Italian Republic delusion); asylum; released August 22; mother's death early next year; inherits Enderby.
- Ch V "The Grave on the Hill": Mildred at Nice; Malcolm Stuart courts Pamela; Vivien's grave at Villefranche (white marble cross, "VIVIEN RANSOME. Died April 24th, 1868. Eternally lamented."); rose cross planted.
- Ch VI "Pamela Changes Her Mind": Castellani at Nice (Hotel Cosmopolitan); Mrs Montagu W. Brown; Pamela drops Castellani for Stuart; Maltravers' letter asks Mildred to Brighton; Pamela to stay with Lady Lochinvar.
- Ch VII "As the Sands Run Down": Mildred at Lewes Crescent; Miss Fausset ill; Mildred visits Enderby churchyard (Greswold at Lola's grave); "George! George!"
- Ch VIII "How Should I Greet Thee?": Greswold cold; Rollinson's curate letters (Frederick Rollinson); Mildred to Enderby; Pamela's engagement & honeymoon at The Hook; Mildred at The Hook (father's study, Mrs Dawson housekeeper).
- Ch IX "Litera Scripta Manet": Mildred finds Fausset's letters in pigeon-hole (red ribbon): Fay born to Fausset's sister Gertrude (Miss Fausset) by Paolo Castellani; sham marriage at Milan; baby Fanny/Fay; £30,000 India Stock deed-of-gift; Mildred sends letter to aunt; returns to Enderby.
- Ch X "Marked by Fate": Mildred returns to Greswold; heart weakness; Dr Porter; Dr Jenner/Clark consult; mother died at 34 of heart disease.
- Ch XI "Like a Tale That Is Told": Pamela's wedding in Westminster Abbey; Miss Fausset's deathbed confession; Mildred inherits; Greswold Hospital; Castellani's decline.

## BOOK 2 of 2: "Cities in the Air" (Edmond Hamilton, Air Wonder Stories, 1929; Gutenberg 74171)

- Captain Martin Brant, American Federation Air-Cruiser 3885; first officer Macklin; second officer Hilliard. Chief of the American Federation: First Air Chief Yarnall; Second Air Chief at San Francisco. Connell (secret agent, prisoner in Berlin).
- Federations: American (New York capital; ~100 air-cities), European (Berlin capital; ~100 cities), Asiatic (Peking capital; ~100 cities).
- Ch I: War declared; cruisers race from NY; Yarnall's briefing; New York city of the air (5-mile disk, 5000 ft tall); air-forts; Great Conference.
- Ch II: Battle over the Atlantic; trapped; triangle formation; crash into fleet; ambush by cloud-projector air-forts; victory.
- Ch III: Under the sea (cruisers submersible).
- Ch IV: Desperate plan—raid on Berlin; air-mine field through vapor-layer; patrols; Berlin's periscope tower.
- Ch V: Brant, Macklin, Hilliard captured; prisoned 100th story; Connell reveals secret: new horizontal tube-propellers allow cities to move at hundreds of mph.
- Ch VI: Hilliard's escape plan (guards); Connell & Macklin escape in cruiser; shot down.
- Ch VII: Berlin moves at speed; gathering of 100 European cities; Brant & Hilliard escape by sliding down tower window-ledges with bunk-strip hooks.
- Ch VIII: Escape from Berlin; Macklin & Connell alive (ruse); American ships rescue; Macklin reveals US tube-propellers installed.
- Ch IX–X: Battle of the Air-Cities over NY; cloud-screens; Paris & Lisbon, Omaha, Hong-Kong fall; circle encirclement; Brant's hundred-cruiser counter-raid.
- Ch XI: Brant seizes Berlin's controls, mows down enemy cities' power-towers; Berlin crashes; victory. Epilogue: dawn, Yarnall: "earth's last air war"; New York flies east "a world at peace."
